credit.zh: 原创示意图（目录级模型）

zh.principle: **标准**：分组密码算法标准（Encryption algorithms — Part 3: Block ciphers）。ISO/IEC 18033-3:2010 规定的是分组密码原语，不规定工作模式。通用接口写成 \(C=E_K(P)\)、\(P=D_K(C)\)，且 \(|P|=|C|=b\)。标准把七种算法分成两族：64 位块为 TDEA、MISTY1、CAST-128、HIGHT；128 位块为 AES、Camellia、SEED。TDEA 的组合写成 \(C=E_{K_3}(D_{K_2}(E_{K_1}(P)))\)，即 EDE 三次 DES；AES 的一轮写成先 SubBytes、ShiftRows、MixColumns，再加轮密钥，轮数由密钥长度决定：128 位密钥 10 轮、192 位 12 轮、256 位 14 轮。
zh.why: 这条卡首先是一次目录纠错：旧目录把 ISO/IEC 18033-3 标成“流密码算法标准”、domain 写成 `d06-otp-stream`，把 Part 3 与 Part 4 的领域对调了。ISO/IEC 18033-3 实际是 block ciphers，ISO/IEC 18033-4 才是 stream ciphers。公式化的意义不在于再讲一遍 AES，而在于把“七种算法、两种块长、三种密钥长度、TDEA 的 EDE 组合、AES 的轮数”放进同一张可核对的表；目录标题、domain 和先修关系必须与这张表一致。
zh.used: 工程上先按数据寿命选块长：新系统优先 128 位块；只有互操作旧协议时才考虑 64 位块。再按安全目标选密钥长度，TDEA 的 128 位密钥是 2-key（有效 112 位），192 位是 3-key（有效 168 位），不能把“密钥位数”直接当“安全强度”。选定原语后必须进入 ISO/IEC 10116 的模式层：CBC 需要不可预测 IV，CTR/GCM 需要唯一 nonce，GCM 还要额外认证数据；本标准本身不提供这些。
zh.broken: 边界有四条。第一，标准只定义原语，不定义模式、填充、IV 生成或认证，拿它直接拼“加密方案”会漏掉完整性。第二，64 位块在约 \(2^{32}\) 个块后出现生日碰撞界，长数据或高并发下不应继续使用 TDEA/MISTY1/CAST-128/HIGHT。第三，TDEA 的 2-key 有效强度约 112 位，3-key 约 168 位，不能按 128/192 位宣称。第四，标准不评估实现侧信道、密钥存储或协议拼接；这些必须另做审计。
zh.history:
ISO/IEC 18033-3 的 2005 年版规定 TDEA、MISTY1、CAST-128、AES、Camellia、SEED；2010 年第二版加入 HIGHT，形成“四种 64 位块 + 三种 128 位块”。AES 来自 FIPS 197，Camellia 与 SEED 是亚洲标准化中广泛使用的 128 位块算法，MISTY1、CAST-128、HIGHT 则保留在 64 位块族。这里只按 ISO 摘要与预览 PDF 的算法表和密钥长度表叙述，不把“列入标准”误写成“仍然推荐”。

**技术参数与复算边界**

该条目的形式模型是 \(S=\min_i S_i,\quad S_i\in\{\text{密钥强度},\text{分组安全},\text{实现安全}\}\)。输入：输入：分组密码算法标准的公开参数、密钥/随机数与消息；变量说明：S 为综合安全强度；各分量取最小值，不能只看密钥位数。 预期输出：按 分组密码算法标准 的规范执行后得到可验证的输出或可比较的优势界。 复算必须给出输入、步骤、输出和单位；示例只演示流程，不替代标准测试向量。

复杂度由密钥长度、分组/状态规模、轮数、随机数质量和敌手模型共同决定；参数越界、版本差异与实现侧信道都可能使公式结论失效。已登记限制：该条目只给出形式模型与可复算步骤，不声称已完成生产实现、侧信道认证或第三方安全评估。

en.principle: **Standard**: Encryption algorithms — Part 3: Block ciphers (分组密码算法标准). ISO/IEC 18033-3:2010 specifies block-cipher primitives, not modes. The generic interface is \(C=E_K(P)\), \(P=D_K(C)\) with \(|P|=|C|=b\). Seven algorithms form two families: 64-bit blocks TDEA, MISTY1, CAST-128 and HIGHT; 128-bit blocks AES, Camellia and SEED. TDEA is \(C=E_{K_3}(D_{K_2}(E_{K_1}(P)))\), the EDE composition of three DES calls. One AES round applies SubBytes, ShiftRows and MixColumns, then AddRoundKey; the number of rounds is 10 for a 128-bit key, 12 for 192 and 14 for 256.
en.why: In the d08-block-ciphers reading path, Encryption algorithms — Part 3: Block ciphers connects to government contexts; the main risks are protocol, implementation.
en.used:
In engineering, choose the block size from data lifetime first: new systems should prefer 128-bit blocks and keep 64-bit blocks for legacy interoperability. Then choose the key size from the security target. TDEA with a 128-bit key is 2-key (about 112-bit strength); 192-bit is 3-key (about 168-bit), so key bits are not the same as security strength. After choosing the primitive, enter the ISO/IEC 10116 mode layer: CBC needs an unpredictable IV, CTR/GCM needs a unique nonce, and GCM also needs additional authenticated data. This standard supplies none of those by itself.

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken: There are four boundaries. First, the standard defines primitives only; it does not define modes, padding, IV generation or authentication, so treating it as a complete encryption scheme loses integrity. Second, a 64-bit block reaches a birthday collision bound near \(2^{32}\) blocks; TDEA, MISTY1, CAST-128 and HIGHT should not carry new long-lived or high-volume data. Third, 2-key TDEA is about 112-bit strength and 3-key about 168-bit; do not advertise 128/192-bit strength. Fourth, the standard does not assess implementation side channels, key storage or protocol composition; those need separate audits.
en.history: The 2005 edition specified TDEA, MISTY1, CAST-128, AES, Camellia and SEED; the 2010 second edition added HIGHT, giving four 64-bit and three 128-bit algorithms. AES comes from FIPS 197; Camellia and SEED are widely used 128-bit block ciphers from Asian standardization; MISTY1, CAST-128 and HIGHT remain in the 64-bit family. The account follows the ISO abstract and the preview algorithm/key-length table, and does not turn “listed in a standard” into “still recommended”.
